messages:
acme-devops: running the private installer in our VPC. model pulls fail and telemetry never reaches Redwood. we see TLS errors and DNS timeouts. anyone seen this pattern?

alex_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error from the installer logs and one curl/nslookup output? that helps narrow DNS vs TLS vs firewall.

acme-devops: here's the curl from the host that fails: 

acme-devops: ```
$ curl -v https://telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net/api/v1/ping
* Rebuilt URL to: https://telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net/api/v1/ping
*   Trying 10.23.45.67...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net (10.23.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* SSL connection using TLS1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* server certificate verification failed: certificate has unknown CA
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) server certificate verification failed: certificate has unknown CA

$ nslookup telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net
Server: 172.31.0.2
Address: 172.31.0.2#53

Non-authoritative answer:
Name: telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net
Address: 10.23.45.67
```

maria_se: thanks — that looks like a TLS interception / MITM (corporate proxy) or missing CA trust. do you have an egress proxy terminating TLS? also, does your VPC use a split-horizon DNS that rewrites redwood endpoints?

acme-devops: we do have a corporate proxy for outbound, and our security team says they intercept TLS for inspection. is there a recommended allowlist and SNI/domain list so we can bypass inspection for critical endpoints?

john_ops: if TLS is intercepted you'll need to either 1) add our telemetry & auth endpoints to your proxy bypass list (recommended), or 2) install our root CA into your host truststore (less ideal). bypass is preferable for keying & KMS.

alex_support: to be explicit, here's the minimal egress allowlist we ask customers to permit for Private installer and runtime model pulls. allow outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDNs (SNI must match, do not rewrite TLS):

alex_support: - telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net
alex_support: - auth.redwood-inference.net
alex_support: - model-registry-us-east-1.redwood-inference.net
alex_support: - storage-us-east-1.redwood-inference.net (S3 gateway IPs)
alex_support: - pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip packages)
alex_support: - deb.debian.org, security.ubuntu.com (apt packages, if using Debian/Ubuntu)
alex_support: - crl3.digicert.com and ocsp.digicert.com (OCSP/CRL checks)
alex_support: - kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (if using AWS KMS-backed keys)
alex_support: - registry-auth.redwood-inference.net (model auth token exchange)

alex_support: ports: 443 (outbound). For some CDNs we also recommend outbound 80 for initial HTTP->HTTPS redirects.

maria_se: additionally, if you use private model shards we may call back to S3-compatible endpoints in other regions; please allow the model-registry-*.redwood-inference.net pattern for the regions you configure. But do not wildcard to *.s3.amazonaws.com unless you can scope to our account IDs/IP ranges — ask your infra team.

acme-devops: can you share IP ranges as a backup? our firewall rules work on IPs only.

john_ops: we generally avoid pushing IPs because CDNs change. but as a short-term workaround we can provide a small set of known IPs for the region. i'll open a ticket for netops to give you a list and advise on TTL checks. for long-term, SNI allowlist / proxy bypass is best.

acme-devops: also seeing failures pulling wheels from our pip mirror when installer runs inside an init container. curl gives TLS alert: handshake failure.

alex_support: that again points to TLS interception or custom CA not trusted by the container base image. quick repro steps to validate:

alex_support: 1) on failing host run: curl -v --resolve telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net:443:10.23.45.67 https://telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net/api/v1/ping
alex_support: 2) openssl s_client -connect telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net:443 -servername telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -subject

acme-devops: ran the openssl, got issuer CN=Corp TLS Inspect CA, subject CN=telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net. company proxy is rewriting cert.

maria_se: OK — need bypass. we'll also recommend you add the following domains to your allowlist for the installer health checks and telemetry:

maria_se: - telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net/api/v1/ping (health)
maria_se: - registry-auth.redwood-inference.net/token (auth exchange)
maria_se: - model-registry-us-east-1.redwood-inference.net/manifest (model metadata)

maria_se: note: for package installs include the IP ranges for the regional pip CDN if your firewall requires IPs — contact support and we'll generate a one-time snapshot of CDN IPs for your region.

acme-devops: one more issue: installer fails when validating signed manifests — error says signature verification failed. could that be caused by TLS interception?

alex_support: yes, if the proxy re-signs responses or modifies payloads. signature verification happens after TLS, so payload tampering will fail verification. Bypass the proxy for model-registry endpoints.

deploy-bot: automated note: raised internal ticket INF-9243 to provide ACME IP snapshot and coordinate with netops. assigned to john_ops. ETA 2 business days.

john_ops: john_ops here — i'll DM netops and pull a current IP snapshot for the us-east-1 artifacts/cdn endpoints, will also add notes about SNI bypass. acme-devops, can you confirm whether your environment allows configuring proxy bypass rules by FQDN or only by IP?

acme-devops: we can do FQDN bypass for HTTPS on the proxy for a specific auth group. we'll request the security exemption. thanks, sending our change ticket to you in a bit.

maria_se: one last configuration tip: the installer has env vars to skip OCSP checks in completely airgapped test envs (REDWOOD_INSTALLER_OCSP=skip) — do NOT use that in production; instead fix TLS path.

acme-devops: noted. big help — we'll attempt bypass and report back. thanks all :raised_hands:

alex_support: ping us once you have the bypass applied. if you want, include a small test script: 

alex_support: ```sh
for host in telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.net registry-auth.redwood-inference.net model-registry-us-east-1.redwood-inference.net; do
  echo "--- $host ---"
  curl -I --silent --show-error https://$host/api/health || true
done
```

acme-devops: will run that after change. thanks.

alex_support: marking this thread as triaged. if bypass doesn't resolve, we'll schedule a short debug call and capture packet traces.

acme-devops: thanks again, will update shortly.
